properties.headline: Special Marine Warning issued September 5 at 7:53PM EDT until September 5 at 9:00PM EDT by NWS Wilmington NC
properties.description:
SMWILM

The National Weather Service in Wilmington has issued a

* Special Marine Warning for...
Coastal waters from Cape Fear NC to Little River Inlet SC out 20
NM...
Coastal waters from Little River Inlet to Murrells Inlet SC out 20
NM...
Coastal waters from Murrells Inlet to South Santee River SC out 20
NM...
Coastal waters from Surf City to Cape Fear NC out 20 nm...
Waters from Little River Inlet SC to South Santee River SC from 20
to 60 NM...
Waters from Surf City NC to Little River Inlet SC from 20 to 60
NM...

* Until 900 PM EDT.

* At 753 PM EDT, strong thunderstorms were located along a line
extending from 21 nm east of Wr2 to 7 nm east of Mount Dirfy's
Wreck to near Belky Bear, moving southeast at 20 knots.

HAZARD...Wind gusts to 40 knots and small hail.

SOURCE...Radar.

IMPACT...Small craft could be damaged in briefly higher winds and
suddenly higher waves.

* Locations impacted include...
Wreck 33, Atlantic Ledge, Little River Offshore Reef, Myrtle Beach
Rock, Frying Pan Shoals Buoy, City Of Houston, Gary Ennis Reef,
Frying Pan Shoals Light Tower, Jungle, Raritan Wreck, Belky Bear,
Wr4, Cherry Grove Inlet, Sherman Wreck, Long Bay Terrace, Bill
Perry Junior Reef, Bp 25 Liberty Ship Wreck, Cape Fear Knuckle
Buoy, Sunset Mid Shelf Buoy, and Mount Dirfy's Wreck.
properties.instruction:
Boaters should seek safe harbor immediately until these storms pass.
If caught on the open water, prepare for deteriorating conditions.
Make sure you and your crew are wearing properly fitted life jackets.

Frequent lightning is occurring with these storms. If caught on the
open water stay below deck if possible, keep away from ungrounded
metal objects.

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued September 5 at 6:30PM MDT until September 5 at 9:30PM MDT by NWS Cheyenne WY
properties.description:
FFWCYS

The National Weather Service in Cheyenne has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
East Central Morrill County in the panhandle of Nebraska...

* Until 930 PM MDT.

* At 630 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain across the warned area. Between 2.5 and 3 inches of rain
have fallen. Additional rainfall amounts up to 1.5 inches are
possible in the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected
to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Broadwater.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued September 5 at 10:18AM CDT until September 6 at 9:34PM CDT by NWS Lake Charles LA
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning is extended for the following rivers in Texas...

Neches River at Neches River Saltwater Barrier affecting Jasper,
Orange, Jefferson and Hardin Counties.

Village Creek Near Kountze affecting Hardin County.

Pine Island Bayou Near Sour Lake affecting Jefferson and Hardin
Counties.

For the Neches River...including Town Bluff, Evadale, Neches River
Saltwater Barrier...Minor flooding is forecast.
For the Village Creek...including Kountze...Minor flooding is
forecast.
For the Pine Island Bayou...including Sour Lake...Minor flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Village Creek near Kountze.

* WHEN...Until Sunday evening.

* IMPACTS...At 20.0 feet, Water begins to flow over the bridge on
Farm to Market Road 418. Water also begins to cover F.M. 418 at
several other locations. Road in Village Creek State Park begins to
have water across it.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 9:30 AM CDT Saturday the stage was 20.7 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 12.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 9:30 AM CDT Saturday was 21.8 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to fall below flood stage late
tomorrow morning and continue falling to 6.8 feet Thursday
morning.
- Flood stage is 17.0 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 20.8
feet on 01/09/1998.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued this evening at 1030 PM CDT.
